title: Check the twelve zodiac centres for a Voynich word paired with a month annotation
statement: I inspected all twelve zodiac centres in the Beinecke MS 408 Yale scans. I looked inside the innermost ring and treated its circumferential inscription as running text. Canvas IDs under https://collections.library.yale.edu/manifests/oid/2002046/canvas/ are 1006200 for f70v2, 1006201 for f70v1, 1006202 for f71r, 1006203 for f71v and f72r1–3, 1006204 for f72v3–2, 1006205 for f72v1, and 1006206–7 for f73r–v. I found a Latin-script month annotation at each emblem and only one freestanding Voynich string in the centres, next to the upper star on f70v2 and separated from mars by the upper fish. This agrees with the earlier dissent on N-001. In f73r and f73v the month writing approaches the circular text, but I saw no particular circumferential word singled out as its counterpart. Zandbergen's month-name table (https://www.voynich.nu/writing.html#zodiac) proposes a later hand and favors Northern French. Cheshire's open 2019 text, figs. 48–50 (https://research-information.bris.ac.uk/ws/files/201563069/Full_text_PDF_accepted_author_manuscript_.pdf), discusses mars, abril and may and proposes a contemporaneous annotator. My scan check addresses position. It leaves the dating and precise spellings open. None of the twelve centres yielded an image-supported pairing between an explicit Voynich word and the month name.
check: Use the cited Yale canvases to locate each inner disk. Independently mark any text inside the disk, whatever its script, and separately mark the circumferential inscription. Record the nearest image object for every standalone Voynich label and any direct connection to the Latin-script month annotation. Have a second reviewer check each candidate on the scan before it is used as an anchor.
